PI Name: Meik Wiking (wiking@happinessresearchinstitute.com)

Co-Investigators: Camilla Michalski (michalski@happinessresearchinstitute.com)

Micah Kaats (kaats@happinessresearchinstitute.com)

PI & Co-Investigator Institution: The Happiness Research Institute

Project Title: What matters for wellbeing?

Section 1: Prior Work & Qualifications
The research team at HRI has designed and carried out, from conception to dissemination, a number of wellbeing studies (e.g., work and wellbeing, happiness in retirement, migrant wellbeing, etc.). These studies have targeted participants residing within and outside of the EU, ranging from 18 years of age to over 75 years, involving both passive and/or active survey data collection covering wellbeing themes similar to that of this study. With this, HRI has a plethora of experience collecting, storing, handling, and disseminating participant data while maintaining strict data privacy and confidentiality standards.

 

Section 2: Project Summary/Design

The primary goal of the study is to investigate whether the process of documenting and reviewing memories can improve wellbeing (and if so, to investigate possible mechanisms such as behavioural changes). Secondary goals include quantifying the extent to which other behavioural and environmental factors can predict wellbeing. Thus, a number of lifestyle and environmental measures will be analyzed in relation to both memory recall activities and reported wellbeing. To accomplish these goals, HRI is partnering with Avicenna Research to run an ecological momentary assessment study in which participants are surveyed daily at regular intervals about their subjective wellbeing, social circumstances, and daily activities. To participate, individuals must be over the age of 18, have no diagnosed/currently treated mental health condition, and have an iPhone running on iOS17.

See also the attached Word document, which contains the text for all the boxes throughout the rest of the document where the text overflows.

Best,

Camilla
